name: Wenzhou Longwan International Airport
before:
Wenzhou's airport, 24 km south east of the city in Zhejiang, and thirty fifth busiest in mainland China with 13,058,523 passengers in 2025.

The terminal arrangement is being rearranged, so check before quoting. Terminal 2, four times the size of Terminal 1 and built for 13 million passengers, takes domestic flights, with Terminal 1 becoming a dedicated international terminal. Terminal 2 also anchors the Wenzhou Comprehensive Transportation Hub, which brings a long distance bus terminal and a subway station onto the same site.

A third phase is under way and it is a big one. Roughly 10.97 billion yuan is being spent to lift capacity from about 13 million passengers to 30 million by 2030, with a second runway of 3,600 metres alongside the existing 3,200 metre one, 50 more aircraft stands and a cargo facility handling 320,000 tonnes a year. The airport is also to be linked directly to Wenzhou East railway station.

The airport can take aircraft up to a 767 or A330. It was called Wenzhou Yongqiang until April 2013.
after:
Wenzhou's airport, 24 km south east of the city in Zhejiang. It was the 35th busiest in mainland China in 2025, with 13,058,523 passengers. Its former name is Wenzhou Yongqiang Airport.

International flights use Terminal 1 and domestic flights Terminal 2. Terminal 2 sits beside the airport's transport hub, which brings long-distance coaches onto the same site.

A third phase of building is being prepared to take the airport to 30 million passengers a year by 2030, with a second runway of 3,600 m beside the existing 3,200 m one and cargo space for 320,000 tonnes a year. The plan also links the airport to Wenzhou East, a planned high-speed railway station.

claims.claim: terminal arrangement being rearranged; check before quoting
claims.wasBefore: The terminal arrangement is being rearranged, so check before quoting.

claims.claim: Terminal 2 four times the size of Terminal 1, built for 13 million
claims.wasBefore: Terminal 2, four times the size of Terminal 1 and built for 13 million passengers, takes domestic flights, with Terminal 1 becoming a dedicated international terminal.
claims.why: Reworded: the split is kept with the operator as the second source. 'Four times the size' and the 13 million design figure for Terminal 2 rest on Wikipedia alone (Wenzhou Daily gives 13 million as the whole airport's design capacity, not Terminal 2's).

claims.claim: hub brings a long distance bus terminal and a subway station onto the site
claims.wasBefore: Terminal 2 also anchors the Wenzhou Comprehensive Transportation Hub, which brings a long distance bus terminal and a subway station onto the same site.
claims.why: Reworded: the hub and its coaches are kept (operator, Wenzhou Daily). The subway station is part of the hub's plans in Wenzhou Daily's 2023 report; no source says it is open.

claims.claim: third phase under way; 10.97 billion yuan; 13 to 30 million; 50 more stands
claims.wasBefore: A third phase is under way and it is a big one. Roughly 10.97 billion yuan is being spent to lift capacity from about 13 million passengers to 30 million by 2030, with a second runway of 3,600 metres alongside the existing 3,200 metre one, 50 more aircraft stands and a cargo facility handling 320,000 tonnes a year.
claims.why: Reworded: the 30 million target, the second runway and the cargo capacity are kept with Wenzhou Daily as the second source. The cost and the 50 stands rest on Wikipedia alone, and 'under way' overstates it: the operator's 2025 record shows the project still in approvals.

claims.claim: linked directly to Wenzhou East railway station
claims.wasBefore: The airport is also to be linked directly to Wenzhou East railway station.
claims.why: Reworded: the station is itself still planned (Wenzhou Daily).

claims.wasBefore: The airport can take aircraft up to a 767 or A330.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone; the operator's page gives the airfield class (4E) but no aircraft limit.
